subject: Pre-QBR: roadmap health, timeline adjustments, and delivery risks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pre-QBR readiness: roadmap health & target launch windows

Team —

High-level snapshot ahead of Friday’s QBR: I pulled the latest delivery numbers and updated the readiness slides (attached). This note summarizes where we are by product area and the decisions I think we need from leadership tomorrow during the run-through.

Quick summary (by area):
- Core API (v2.3): feature complete; integration tests failing on long-sequence caching in 4% of runs. Target release: 2026-12-08 (nominal).
- Embeddings service: stable; finishing quantization validation. Target release: 2026-12-01 (on-track).
- Dedicate infra autoscaling: still blocked by container image signing (security). Target release: 2026-12-15 (risk: medium-high).

Top delivery risks to highlight in QBR:
1) Long-sequence KV-cache regression: intermittent correctness issues causing degraded responses for 8k+ token sessions. Root cause points to cache eviction race under high concurrency. Impact: customer-facing latency/regression for batch workloads.
2) Container signing dependency: legal/security pipeline requires image signing for Dedicated; release is gated until partner signing is validated. No alternate path without an SLA exception.
3) Docs + SDK sync: small but visible surface-area mismatch in SDKs (Python/Go); causes errors for early adopters on Dedicated.

Decisions requested:
- Approve 2-week contingency buffer for Core API go-live OR sign off to proceed with partial rollout (embeddings on, core on canary).
- Approve temporary SLA exception for Dedicated if partner signing cannot be verified by 2026-12-05.
- Confirm owner for customer comms (Acme) if we need to slip their pilot window.

Attachments included: pre-qbr-readiness-slides.pdf (deck), feature-compatibility-matrix.csv (matrix).

Next steps: would like a short leadership sync at 16:00 PT to confirm the contingency approach and final slides. Please skim the deck before then; I’ve highlighted the 1-slide risk cards for each area.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Folks —

Brief technical update and proposed mitigations for the KV-cache regression: 

What we see: under sustained concurrency (200+ concurrent sessions with >4k tokens) a window opens where cache eviction and writeback can interleave leading to stale pointers. Repro rate ~1 in 250 on the internal stress harness.

Immediate mitigations (can ship in 48–72h):
- Option A (fast): Introduce a lightweight eviction lock around cache buckets + conservative TTL increase. Pros: short turnaround (48–72h), reduces repro rate by ~95%. Cons: small latency hit (~5–8% median).
- Option B (fallback): Canary mode that degrades to per-request recompute past 4k tokens while leaving behavior unchanged for typical sessions. Pros: no risk to correctness for long sessions; Cons: increases token cost and latency for those sessions.

Longer-term (2–3 weeks): rework concurrency path and add deterministic tests in CI.

Attachments: kv-cache-optimizations.patch, latency-benchmarks.xlsx

If leadership agrees to a 2-week contingency buffer, Option A + canary rollout seems like the balanced route: quick reduction in repro, minimal customer exposure, follow-up full fix post-release.

Karthik
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

I approve a 2-week contingency buffer for the Core API go-live, conditional on engineering owning the rollback playbook and a short customer communication plan for Acme.

Laura — please draft a short public-facing paragraph for Acme (neutral tone, no firm dates) and circulate by 17:30 PT. Marcus, Karthik — feed the 1-slide risk card and the two-line mitigation description into the deck so we can move to final slides.

I’ll be on the 16:00 leadership pre-brief.
